svg.title: How the Reasoning Graph Local Simplification Algorithm Works
svg.desc: Seven-step animated demonstration of ReasoningFlow deterministic browser-local reduction. Using the document's OpenAI example, 44 original nodes are grouped into 30 consecutive, source-linked nodes; endpoint protection, run allocation, TF-IDF and cosine grouping, adjacent merges, projection of original relationships, ELK layout and browser caching are visualized. The seven-stage animation auto-plays once, holds on the final frame, and includes optional controls when viewed as a standalone SVG.
svg.text: How a reasoning graph gets simpler
Local reduction: consecutive groups, preserved evidence, and no model summarization calls.

g.text: The actual algorithm switches to grouping only when the source graph has more than 30 nodes.
Keep every node and every edge
Endpoint protection follows the first and last generated reasoning/research nodes.
Tool records can appear afterward: U40 is protected even though U41–U43 follow it.
Start with one slot per interval; distribute the remaining slots by flexible-run capacity.
Floors + largest remainders decide extra slots. Unused slots are not redistributed later.
TF-IDF turns source slices into sparse vectors; cosine controls the first forward pass.
The first pass compares a unit only with the last group—not with earlier matching topics.
Schematic vectors and decisions; unit-level similarity scores are not published in the case study.

g.text: Internal relationships disappear from the compact view; equivalent external arrows aggregate.

u1 → u2 → u3 become internal: hidden from compact drawing
